title: Left to Look After Itself
logline: On the last working day before the northeast monsoon shuts the one-kilometre crossing for months, the small staff of an offshore marine reserve take the boardwalk up in sections, shutter the hut, unbolt the signs, drain the tank, leave a number with the boat owners on the beach, count the days on a calendar, and go, leaving behind a reef nobody will be able to look at.
human_question: What do you owe to the things you are about to be unable to reach?

place.what_kind_of_place: A pair of granite outcrops joined by a low sand spit, a kilometre off a long east-coast beach, with a fringing coral reef on the sheltered side that shows through the water as clearly as if it were drawn. On the island itself: wild rock doves nesting in the cracks of the boulders, sea-blown scrub in the hollows, a short boardwalk laid on the sand to keep feet off it, a one-room warden's hut with shutters, a plastic water tank on a frame, a stack of bolted signboards about anchoring and about what not to stand on, two or three mooring buoys, and a rubbish drum. Nothing on it is generating anything, storing anything or worth stealing. On the mainland shore opposite: a beach office with a ticket counter and a shutter, a radio, a logbook, a range office up the road, and a line of small outboard boats belonging to families in the village who take visitors across in the calm half of the year and do other things in the other half. Between the two, a kilometre of water that is flat and turquoise for five months and, for the rest, a following sea with wind on it that no small boat crosses.
place.why_it_is_worth_watching: Because the place produces one frame that is also the whole of the idea. From height, the island sits inside its own reef with the reef legible under the water, and on this particular day there is a single wake leading away from it towards the mainland and nothing else moving anywhere in the picture. That shot is beautiful before it means anything and it is the film's entire statement: everything that could be settled has been settled, and what is left has been left. Close, the day is a list of small, unheroic, entirely practical acts, each one about something that cannot look after itself: boardwalk sections lifted, numbered and stacked above the tide line; shutters screwed down; a tank emptied and turned over; signboards unbolted and carried to the boat because next season they must be here to be read; a buoy hauled and the line coiled; the drum emptied; the hut swept; a last walk round the spit picking up what the sea will otherwise take out into the reef. Then a logbook entry, a form signed, a number written on a piece of card and left with the boat owners, and a calendar with a date circled on it that nobody in the frame chose.
place.what_moves_or_changes: On the island, nothing at all for months, which is the point. Everything that changes on this day changes because somebody carried it. On the water, everything: the crossing that has been routine since June becomes impossible within a fortnight, and it is the sea and not any person that decides when it is possible again. The reef goes on doing what reefs do, unobserved, and is exposed to exactly the things the staff are there to prevent, which is why the securing matters and why it is not enough. On the shore the change is small and domestic: boats hauled further up the sand, engines taken off and carried home, a shutter down, and the same families turning to whatever else the wet months are for.
place.when_it_looks_best: The hinge of the season, which is the one week the film exists in: the last calm days before the northeast monsoon sets in, when the water is still clear enough for the reef to read from height and the wind has already begun to arrive in the afternoons. Within the day, the island wants the first hour, when the light is flat across the spit and the reef has no glare on it, and the last hour for the crossing back. A single return visit in the middle of the closed months, filmed from the mainland shore with the island invisible behind rain, would give the film the one thing this week cannot: the length of the absence.

two_layers.without_the_philosophy: A film about closing a small place up for the winter. Boardwalk sections lifted and numbered; shutters screwed down; a water tank emptied and turned over; signboards unbolted; a buoy hauled and its line coiled; a drum emptied; a last walk round a sand spit picking up plastic; a logbook filled in; a number written on card and handed to a man with a boat; a date circled on a calendar; and a single boat crossing back with four people and a stack of signs in it. Then a beach with the boats further up it than they were, and rain coming. It has a complete shape with nothing said over it, and anyone who likes the end of a season, or careful packing, or a place that is about to be left alone, has a whole piece here.
two_layers.with_the_philosophy: The same day becomes the four preliminary duties the sources attach to the deepest withdrawal they describe. Before a practitioner stops completely for a period fixed in advance, the texts have him do four very ordinary things: make safe the belongings that are not on his body; make himself answerable to his community, whose call is strong enough to end the withdrawal; make himself answerable to his teacher; and check honestly how much of his life is left, because what he is about to do cannot postpone his death. A day spent making a place safe before being unable to reach it puts all four on screen without anybody reciting them. The voice is exact about what it is not saying. Nobody here is entering anything. The state the sources describe is restricted to rare people already free, ordinary people cannot enter it, it is not switching off and not a rest, and it is not what a closed island is. And at the one point where the film's subject looks most like an arrival — a boat leaving an island empty — the voice says plainly that the peace these texts finally point at has no place, no direction and no shape, that nobody travels to it, and that no shot in this film or any other is a picture of it.

sequence.on_screen: First light, high above the strait. The island inside its own reef, the reef legible through the water, the sand spit between the two rocks, the mainland beach a kilometre off with a line of small boats on it. One boat is crossing out.
sequence.voice: The sources describe a withdrawal more complete than anything else in them: a stop, entered on purpose, for a length of time fixed before it begins, in which not one moment of mind occurs [C102-P:L29]. And immediately before the stop they have the practitioner do four things that are not spiritual at all. They are about property, about other people, about a superior, and about a date [C102-P:L43–L62].

sequence.on_screen: The first duty, done at working speed. Boardwalk sections lifted, numbered in chalk and stacked above the tide line. Shutters screwed down on the hut. A water tank emptied and turned over on its frame. Signboards unbolted and carried across the sand to the boat. A mooring buoy hauled and its line coiled on the deck. A rubbish drum emptied. A last walk round the spit picking up what the sea would otherwise carry into the reef.
sequence.voice: The first duty is the plainest. Make safe the things that are not on your body, because you will not be able to reach them [C102-P:L50]. Everything being carried down this beach is here for the same reason: it cannot be repaired from the mainland, it cannot be replaced by anyone before the crossing opens again, and the sea will take whatever is left loose.

sequence.on_screen: Ashore, the paperwork. A logbook filled in at the beach office counter. A form signed at the range office up the road, dated. A number written on a piece of card in block capitals and handed to a man standing by an outboard, who folds it into his shirt pocket without comment.
sequence.voice: The second and third duties are about being reachable. The practitioner makes himself answerable to his community and to his teacher, and the text is specific about why: if the community needs him, it will send someone, and the call will certainly be answered, because a community deserves that much [C102-P:L54]. This is not a withdrawal that cuts anybody off. It is arranged so that the people with a claim on you still have one.

sequence.on_screen: A wall calendar in the beach office with a date ringed in pen, and a tide table beside it. Somebody counting weeks with a finger. Then the same office window, and outside it the water already carrying wind lines that were not there a fortnight ago.
sequence.voice: The sources treat real skill in any of these states as four things: going in, staying, coming out at the time you chose, and looking back over it afterwards [C099-P:L69–L79]. The last of those is where this day and the texts part company, and the film should say so. Nobody on this beach chooses the date they come back. The sea chooses it, and the ring on that calendar is a guess.

sequence.on_screen: The reef from directly overhead, in clear flat light, with nobody on it and nothing in the water. A broken branch of coral lying pale on the sand. Then the empty mooring where the buoy was.
sequence.voice: The fourth duty is the hardest of the four. The practitioner is to work out honestly how much of his life remains, because what he is about to enter cannot be used to postpone anything: the text says in as many words that death is not prevented by it [C102-P:L58; C102-P:L58–L62]. Even the outer limit in the sources is a physical one, tied to how long a body can go without food, and not an endurance record [C102-P:L66]. Securing a place is not the same as protecting it. Nobody will be looking at this reef for four months.

sequence.on_screen: From height, the last crossing. The island inside its reef, one wake leading away from it, nothing else moving anywhere in the frame. Held long. Then the boat becoming small against the mainland beach.
sequence.voice: The film has to stop here and say what it cannot show. What these texts are finally pointing at is not a place. They deny it any location, any direction and any shape, and they are explicit that it is not somewhere a person travels to [C073-P:L62; C073-P:L74]. They also say it is not made by effort at all, only uncovered [C073-P:L20]. So this is a boat leaving an island, and it is a beautiful shot, and it is not a picture of the thing. Nothing a camera can hold is.

sequence.on_screen: Late afternoon on the mainland. Boats hauled further up the sand than they were in the morning, engines carried off on shoulders, the office shutter coming down, the signboards stacked inside against a wall. Men walking away up the road. The first of the weather arriving over the strait.
sequence.voice: Three corrections the sources make themselves. This is not switching off, not a rest and not a retreat from work: it is restricted to rare people who are already free, who have mastered all eight attainments, and ordinary people cannot enter it [C102-P:L31; C102-P:L41; C102-M:L9]. It is not a coma or anything medical: the body stays warm and the senses stay whole [C102-P:L80]. And it ends the way it began, in a single moment, after which ordinary mind simply resumes [C102-P:L68–L70]. What a last working day like this one can show is only the shape of the four duties: that being out of reach honestly means settling, first, everything that cannot follow you.

concept_merge.why_together: C102 carries the film and is unusually filmable. It sets out a withdrawal entered deliberately for a period fixed in advance, in which mind does not occur at all [C102-P:L29], restricted to non-returners and arahants who have mastered all eight attainments [C102-P:L31; C102-P:L41; C102-M:L9], and it places immediately before it four preliminary duties that are entirely practical: protecting the belongings that are not on the body, remaining answerable to the community, remaining answerable to the teacher, and checking how much lifespan is left [C102-P:L43–L62]. It is specific about the community's claim, which is strong enough to end the withdrawal and will certainly be answered [C102-P:L54]; specific that death cannot be prevented by any of it [C102-P:L58]; specific that the outer limit is tied to how long a body lasts without food [C102-P:L66]; specific that the state is not death, because heat, life and the senses remain [C102-P:L80]; and specific about emergence in a single moment of fruition after which ordinary mind resumes [C102-P:L68–L70]. C099 supplies the one honest correction the day needs: the sources' idea of mastery is entering, staying, leaving at a chosen time and reviewing afterwards [C099-P:L69–L79], and on this beach nobody chooses the time, which the film states rather than hides. C073 supplies the boundary at the exact moment the footage is most seductive: the peace the group is finally about is denied any location, direction or shape [C073-P:L62; C073-P:L74] and is realised rather than produced [C073-P:L20], so a boat leaving an empty island is a beautiful shot and not a picture of anything unconditioned. A last working day before a fixed seasonal closure puts all four duties into one afternoon's carrying and paperwork, with no household's livelihood on screen and nobody's inner state claimed.
concept_merge.what_it_reveals: That the deepest withdrawal these texts describe is hedged about with obligations rather than freed from them, and that the obligations are to property, to other people, to a superior and to a clock. Stated flat, the four duties are a list. Put on a day in which a boardwalk is numbered in chalk, a tank is turned over, a number is written on card and handed to a man with a boat, and a date is ringed on a calendar nobody controls, they become a working sequence with a deadline in it. The film also gets the concept's sharpest corrections where the footage can carry them: the community's claim is filmed as a phone number rather than described; the refusal of 'this cannot postpone death' is spoken over a reef that will be unwatched whatever anybody carried off the beach; and the difference between securing something and protecting it is visible in the same frame as the securing. This idea has been round once before. Its first version filmed a fishing family's day before a multi-day trip: that is dropped because the project's digests forbid using the sources' own livelihood examples, fishermen and hunters, to frame real working communities, and because it put a household's debts and arrangements on screen. The concept is unchanged and the subject has moved to an institution's seasonal closure, where the thing left behind is public, nobody's income is the film's material, and the fixed period is set by weather rather than by anybody's need to earn.

concept_links.why: The film is the four preliminary duties and nothing else from the concept. The duty to make safe what is not on the body is narrated over the boardwalk, the shutters, the tank and the signs [C102-P:L50]; the duties of answerability to community and teacher are narrated over a logbook, a signed form and a number handed to a boat owner, with the source's own reason for the community's claim spoken [C102-P:L54]; the duty of checking one's remaining time is narrated over an unwatched reef together with the text's flat statement that death is not prevented by any of this [C102-P:L58; C102-P:L58–L62], and the seven-day limit is given as the physical limit the source ties it to rather than as a feat [C102-P:L66]; and the closing beat carries the framing statement of the whole thing, that it is entered for a period fixed in advance and that no moment of mind occurs in it [C102-P:L29]. Every limit in the digest is honoured and four of them are spoken out loud. Cessation is not presented as switching off, a detox or a nap: the closing beat says the sources restrict it to rare, already-liberated people who have mastered all eight attainments, and that ordinary people cannot enter it [C102-P:L31; C102-P:L41; C102-M:L9]. It is not offered as an escape from responsibility, since the film's whole subject is the responsibilities. It is not offered as a way of postponing anything. It is not linked to coma, sleep, sedation or any medical state: the film says the body stays warm and the senses stay whole [C102-P:L80]. It is not 'emptying the mind', and no practice, breathing, stillness or calm of any kind is filmed. Nobody in the film is entering anything, nobody's composure is presented as an attainment, and the phrase about dwelling at ease here and now is deliberately not spoken over any footage, because there is nothing on screen it could honestly be attached to [C102-P:L92].

One statement of this concept is narrated, and it is narrated against the film rather than for it. The sources' account of mastery is being able to advert, enter, stay, leave at the time one has chosen, and review afterwards [C099-P:L69–L79]; the film speaks that over a calendar with a date ringed on it and then says plainly that nobody on this beach chooses the date, the sea does, which is the film's own limit rather than a parallel. That keeps the digest's clearest warning honoured by construction: a working parallel is at most an echo and never an instance, and no work, craft or routine in this film is presented as absorption. The digest's other limits are honoured too. Nothing here is offered as a happiness technique, and absorption bliss is not mentioned at all, since the film has no meditator and no practice in it [C099-P:L79]. The named preliminary moments are not turned into a four-step programme and are not narrated. The slow and quick counts, and the digest's statement that attainment depends on endowment rather than effort [C099-P:L57], are not used to rank anybody in the frame, and nobody's capability is commented on at all.

This link exists to stop one shot from lying. The film's most beautiful frame is a boat leaving an island empty, and the digest's plainest denials are spoken over it: the peace the texts point at has no location, direction, material or shape, and it is not a place anyone goes to [C073-P:L62; C073-P:L74]; it is realised rather than produced or manufactured [C073-P:L20]. The voice then says in as many words that the shot is not a picture of it and that no shot could be. Every limit in the digest that bears on this film is honoured. It is not presented as a mood, a calm or a relaxation, because no calm is filmed [C073-P:L18]. It is not presented as nothingness or as annihilation, and the empty island is never allowed to stand for an ending. It is not presented as personal or as something anybody creates. The 'with residue' and 'without residue' pair is not used, the five stages are not used, and the three names are not used, because none of them can be attached to anything on screen without faking. The Margaya's argument from what people will pay to be released from debt and illness [C073-M:L7] is not used either: there is no household finance anywhere in this film.

what_the_viewer_could_understand: That the deepest withdrawal this tradition describes comes with four practical duties attached before it can begin: making safe what you cannot reach, staying answerable to your community, staying answerable to your teacher, and knowing honestly how much time you have, because the withdrawal cannot postpone death. That it is entered for a length of time decided in advance and left in a single moment, after which ordinary mind resumes. That the sources restrict it to rare people who are already free and say ordinary people cannot enter it, so it is not switching off, not a rest and not anything a camera can find. And that the peace the group is finally about has no location at all, so an emptied island and a departing boat are an analogy the film names as one and nothing more.
what_must_be_real: The reserve's own closing-up, on its own date, in its own order, with the department's permission. Nothing is unbolted, lifted, stacked, emptied or carried a second time for the camera, no item is put back so that it can be taken down again on a better light, and the day is not moved, extended or rehearsed. If the closure is ragged — a section left, a job not finished, a decision changed — the film keeps that. The staff are filmed as people doing work, are not named or followed as characters, are not asked to comment on any doctrine, and nothing about their composure, patience or care is presented as an attainment or as an echo of one. Nobody sets foot on the reef, nothing is moved on it, nothing is arranged on it, and no marine life is baited, herded or handled for a shot; the film's underwater and overhead material is whatever can be taken without touching anything. The boat owners on the shore are not asked how the closed months affect their income and no household's earnings, debts or season are put on screen. No danger at sea is filmed, staged or implied for effect, and the crew crosses only when the boat would have crossed anyway.
position_hint: second to last in the group, immediately before the film about release: it is the group's statement of what a responsible withdrawal actually costs, and it is the last film in which anything is still being held on to. It also does the group's most important piece of ground-clearing on the way through, by saying out loud, over the shot most likely to be misread, that the unconditioned has no location and cannot be filmed. No location reasoning is involved.
risks: Letting the closure read as a spiritual arrival, so that an emptied island becomes a picture of peace. The film's most beautiful shot is the most dangerous one in it and has to be narrated against.
Letting cessation sound like switching off, a reset, an off-season or a rest, which is the digest's first and firmest correction.
Implying that anybody on screen is entering, approaching or capable of anything the texts describe, or that the staff's steadiness is an echo of an attainment.
Turning the closed months into hardship for the boat families, or into a story about lost income, which would put a community's livelihood on screen as the film's material.
Making the staff into guardians of a mystery, or the closure into a vigil, when it is a day of carrying and paperwork.
Sentimentalising the reef, so that the film becomes an argument about conservation and the four duties become a message about protecting nature.
Letting the film look like a travel piece about a well-known island, which the aerial material makes very easy and which would empty the subject out.
Filming anything that damages the reef: standing on it, anchoring over it, or working close to it for the sake of a shot.
Using the weather for suspense, or crossing in conditions the boat would not have crossed in.
drop_if: The reserve is not in fact closed up on a fixed date, so there is no securing to film and the four duties would have to be staged.
The department will not allow the closing day to be filmed, or will only allow a demonstration of it on another date.
The closure amounts to locking a door, so that nothing that cannot look after itself is actually being made safe.
The overhead and underwater material cannot be obtained without anybody standing on, anchoring over or disturbing the reef.
The crossing cannot be made on the day the staff make it, so the film would have to arrange its own boat and its own day.

connections.note: From a capacity that discharges in two seconds to a whole day of setting things down before anybody can be out of reach.
From securing a place you intend to come back to, to releasing one with nothing kept back and no return arranged.

selection.reason: The four preliminary duties are the most filmable thing in the whole group, and a fixed seasonal closure puts all four of them into one afternoon without a household's livelihood or anybody's inner state being the film's material.

review.note: Rewritten and relocated 2026-09-24. The previous version filmed a fishing family securing the house before a multi-day trip; the family and the fishing are both dropped, because the project's digests forbid using the sources' own livelihood examples, fishermen and hunters, to frame real working communities, and because the old version put a household's debts and arrangements on screen and used the danger of the trip as the film's tension. The concept is untouched and is the strongest in the group for filming: C102's four preliminary duties tie a withdrawal to the safety of property, to the community, to a teacher and to one's own remaining lifespan. The subject is now the last working day before a fixed seasonal closure of an offshore reserve, where what is being made safe is public rather than anybody's home, the fixed period is set by weather rather than by a need to earn, and nobody's income is the film's material. All three concept links are kept, re-tested and rewritten. Every citation was checked against its digest's own evidence before use, including the ranges the digest itself cites rather than the ones a reading of the source might suggest: C102-P:L43–L62 for the four duties, C102-P:L58–L62 and C102-P:L58 for the lifespan clause, C099-P:L69–L79 for the five masteries, and C073-P:L62 with C073-P:L74 for the denial of location. C099 is now used against the film rather than for it: the source's mastery is leaving at a time one chose, and the film says out loud that nobody here chooses the date. C102's phrase about dwelling at ease here and now is deliberately left unspoken, because there is nothing on screen it could honestly sit over. The film's most beautiful frame, a boat leaving an island empty, is narrated with C073's flat denials so that it cannot be read as the unconditioned, and the voice says that no shot in this film or any other is a picture of it.

suggested_location.region: Trincomalee District, Eastern Province: a kilometre off a long beach on the coast north of the harbour town, at the southern end of the island's east-coast monsoon belt
suggested_location.why_here: Because the fixed period is real, the thing left behind is public, and the whole idea is visible in one frame. The park is two granite rocks and a sand spit a kilometre offshore, holding some of the best surviving coral reef in the country; it was a sanctuary from 1963 and a national park from 2003; and the crossing to it is a matter of season rather than of will. The calm half of the year on this coast runs roughly from May to September and small boats cross all day; from about November to February the northeast monsoon puts a sea between the beach and the island that no outboard crosses, and access is suspended. That gives the film exactly what the concept needs and nothing it does not: a date after which nobody can reach the place, known in advance, decided by weather and not by anybody's plan, with a body of ordinary infrastructure on the island that cannot look after itself and cannot be repaired from the mainland. It is also an institution rather than a household. The staff are a department's staff, the signs and the boardwalk and the hut are public property, and no family's income or privacy is the film's material. And the aerial material is unusually good: the reef reads through the water, the island sits inside it, and a single wake leading away from it is both the most beautiful shot the place gives and the clearest statement of the idea.
what_to_film: The island inside its reef from height in flat early light, with the reef legible through the water, the spit between the two rocks, and the mainland beach a kilometre off in the same frame.
The boardwalk being lifted section by section, numbered in chalk and stacked above the tide line.
The hut: shutters screwed down, the floor swept out, the door closed, filmed plainly and at length.
The water tank emptied and turned over on its frame, and the rubbish drum emptied and carried.
Signboards unbolted, carried across the sand and laid in the boat, with the bare bolt holes left behind.
A mooring buoy hauled and its line coiled on the deck.
The last walk round the spit, picking up what the sea would otherwise take into the reef.
Ashore: the logbook at the beach office counter, the signed and dated form at the range office, and a number written on card and handed to a boat owner.
The wall calendar with the date ringed on it and the tide table beside it, close, because it is the one thing in the film nobody controls.
The reef from directly overhead, with nobody on it and nothing in the water, held long.
The last crossing from height: the island, the reef, one wake, and nothing else moving.
The shore afterwards: boats hauled further up the sand, engines carried off, the shutter down, the signs stacked against a wall inside.
One return visit inside the closed months, from the mainland beach, with the island invisible behind weather.
suggested_location.access: The park is reached only by boat from the mainland beach, a crossing of about a kilometre, and everything about filming it depends on written permission from the wildlife department, which administers it, plus whatever clearance the district requires; this is a coast where naval clearance has historically been part of any offshore filming and that should be assumed rather than hoped against. Nothing may be filmed from in or on the reef without the department's specific agreement, and nothing should be filmed there at all if it means standing on coral or anchoring over it. The crew must be able to cross with the staff on the staff's own boat and on the staff's own day, and to come back when they do. Drone flight over a national park needs the department's permission in its own right and cannot be assumed from any general rule. The window is narrow and weather-bound at both ends: too early and there is no closure to film, too late and there is no crossing.
suggested_location.best_time: The hinge of the season, in the last calm days before the northeast monsoon sets in — on the published seasons that is somewhere in October, but the actual date is the department's and the sea's and cannot be fixed months ahead, so the film has to be able to travel on short notice and to wait. Within the day, the first hour for the island and the reef, the working middle for the securing, and the last hour for the crossing back. One separate visit inside the closed months, for the shore in weather, should be planned from the start.

suggested_location.research_note: Desk research only, and unverified on the ground. From the sources above: the park is one of the country's three marine national parks, lies about a kilometre off a mainland coastal town on this coast, covers about 471 hectares, takes its name from the rock pigeon that colonised it, was declared a sanctuary in 1963 and re-designated a national park in 2003 as the seventeenth in the country, holds some of the best remaining coral reef on the island, was used as a shooting range in the colonial period and was among the protected areas damaged by the 2004 tsunami. On the season: the coast is governed by the northeast monsoon from roughly October to March; the island is generally described as accessible from about May or June to September or October, at its busiest in the calm months, and as closing or becoming inaccessible from about November to February, with boat services suspended when the sea is bad. The coordinates are the published position of the island and are not a survey. The largest assumption in this record, and the first thing to check, is the film's whole premise: that the closure is a fixed administrative event with a securing routine attached, rather than simply a period in which boats stop coming. The published sources say the island may close and that services may be suspended; none of them describes a closing-up, a boardwalk, a hut, a tank, signboards, a logbook or a date on a calendar, and every one of those details is inferred from what a small offshore visitor facility in a monsoon belt must plausibly do. If the department simply stops issuing tickets, this film does not exist and should be dropped rather than staged. No officer, boat owner, office or household has been identified or approached, and no permission has been sought from the wildlife department, the navy or anybody else. Two photographs of the island were found on Wikimedia Commons and are used above; no photograph of the shore office, the staff or any part of the closing-up was found.

unknowns: Whether the closure is a fixed administrative event with a securing routine attached, or simply a period in which boats stop crossing — the film's entire premise.
What is actually on the island that has to be made safe, and whether it amounts to more than locking a door.
Whether the wildlife department will permit the closing day itself to be filmed, on its own date, rather than offering a demonstration on a convenient one.
Whether naval or district clearance is required for the crossing and for flight over the park, and whether it can be obtained inside a narrow weather-bound window.
Whether the overhead and underwater material can be obtained without anybody standing on, anchoring over or otherwise disturbing the reef.
Whether the date can be known far enough in advance for a crew to be there, given that it is decided by the sea.
evidence_class_note: Editorial proposal. The location is proposed by Claude from desk research and is unverified. No scene or shot is decided here.
